budget_items.topic: DASH aquatic weed harvesting program, town beach
budget_items.what_was_said: The diver-assisted suction harvesting program at town beach was completed for the season with positive feedback; funding is available in the capital account for a second round next year, or the town could switch to a chemical weed control method under the existing permit.

budget_items.topic: Wallace Park basketball court lighting replacement
budget_items.what_was_said: The town electrician quoted replacing six old mercury lamp fixtures with LEDs, adding a lockable, timer-controlled exterior light switch; the quote covers labor and materials, with any additional work outside scope to be separately discussed and approved. Disposal of the old mercury-containing lamps as hazardous waste was noted as a likely added cost not included in the quote.

budget_items.topic: Green Communities Act funding for lighting project
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner suggested checking whether Green Communities Act funding could offset the lighting upgrade cost rather than drawing further from the revolving account; the chair agreed to look into it.

Current per-child seasonal usage fees for fields have not been adjusted in several years and were described as very low; the commission compared them to the school district's hourly facility usage fee structure and discussed possibly restructuring to an hourly model.

budget_items.topic: Turf field rental rate comparison (French River summer soccer)
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner cited what a neighboring/comparable program charged per hour for turf field use as a benchmark while discussing the town's own fee structure.

Commissioners discussed adding a per-hour lighting surcharge to field/court rental fees if the Wallace Park lights are upgraded, citing a school district figure as a benchmark, and agreed the parks fee could reasonably be set lower.
A one-time-use fee for a resident (e.g., a family reunion using a field for an afternoon) was cited from the existing fee schedule, with a note that the figures may already have been updated since.

budget_items.topic: Municipal grounds maintenance cost by field
budget_items.what_was_said: A cost-per-mowing breakdown by field was shared for context on why user fees exist: figures were given for Fitzgerald, an unclear second field, and Marshall Park's ball field, with other sites (Veterans Park, Town Beach, Wallace Park) noted as having no mowing cost.

decisions.decision: The rec department may continue to reserve library space while the MOU is finalized; a revised draft will be shared and reviewed as a check-off item next month rather than requiring a formal sign-off vote.
Hold off voting on the Wallace Park lighting project until next month, pending answers on the quote timeline, disposal cost, control system, and possible Green Communities Act funding.
Before investing in the Wallace Park lighting upgrade, develop a lighting policy/agenda item addressing hours of use and neighbor notification.
Continue reviewing the field usage fee schedule this fall, aiming to reach a consensus by October or November, with a full commission present before voting.
Next meeting set for September 30th; the following meeting will be October 28th.

minutes.headline: Parks Commission OK'd beach access for a fundraiser and is weighing a $2,200 Wallace Park lighting upgrade
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Parks Commission approved town beach access for a November Polar Plunge fundraiser, heard from the library board of trustees on a draft MOU governing recreation department use of library rooms, and opened discussion -- without voting -- on replacing old mercury lights at Wallace Park's basketball courts and on updating long-unchanged field usage fees. No fee schedule or lighting decision was finalized; both were held for further information and a future meeting.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission approved town beach access for a November 28 Polar Plunge fundraiser.
The commission held off voting on replacing old mercury lights at Wallace Park's basketball courts, pending a quote timeline, disposal cost, and possible state grant funding.
Before committing to that lighting upgrade, the commission wants a policy on hours of use and neighbor notification.
A draft memorandum of understanding on recreation department use of library rooms remains unsigned; a revised draft is due for review next month.
The commission will keep reviewing field and court usage fees this fall, aiming for consensus by October or November.

why_it_matters: A Wallace Park lighting upgrade would likely be paid from the parks revolving account or a Green Communities Act grant rather than the tax levy, but no funding source or cost is settled yet.
Field and court usage fees, described as unchanged for years, could rise for youth sports leagues and residents who rent town fields and courts.
The library-recreation MOU will set the terms under which town recreation programs can keep using library meeting rooms going forward.
